companies.focus: Integrated robot joint modules (harmonic/planetary) and frameless BLDC torque motors for humanoid, collaborative and legged robots, plus dexterous hands.
companies.summary: Leadshine is a Shenzhen-based, publicly listed motion-control manufacturer (founded 1997) that supplies robot joint actuators (HJ2 harmonic and PJ3 joint modules) and FM1/FM2 frameless torque motors as core components for humanoid and collaborative robots.
companies.price_positioning: Mid-range, value-oriented for the humanoid-component market. Few public prices: FM2-class frameless motors list around ~$199 on Leadshine's store; integrated harmonic joint modules (HJ2/PJ3) are not publicly priced but, given the brand's cost-competitive positioning, are expected to undercut premium harmonic-drive actuators (Harmonic Drive, maxon). Rough estimate: frameless motors ~$150-400; integrated joint modules low-hundreds to ~$1k+ depending on size (estimate, not from official price list).

companies.focus: Frameless (housingless) direct-drive BLDC torque motors for robotic joints — paired by the integrator with harmonic/planetary/cycloidal gearing; not pre-integrated QDD modules.

companies.parent: RoboDrive is a product brand of TQ-Systems GmbH, part of the TQ-Group (owner-managed German electronics group, founded 1994 by Detlef Schneider and Rudiger Stahl). RoboDrive frameless-motor technology originated at the German Aerospace Center (DLR) Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics; it was spun off as RoboDrive GmbH (founded 2005), manufactured by TQ-Systems from 2006, and fully integrated into TQ-Systems in 2015.
companies.focus: Frameless (stator-rotor kit) high-torque-density BLDC servo motors (premium ILM and cost-optimized ILM-E series), plus custom integrated actuators, for robotics/cobots/humanoids/medical/aerospace
companies.summary: TQ-RoboDrive is the robotics drive brand of TQ-Systems GmbH, supplying DLR-derived frameless hollow-shaft servo-motor kits (premium ILM and cost-optimized ILM-E series) and custom integrated actuators with market-leading torque density for cobots, humanoids, exoskeletons, and medical/aerospace robots.
companies.price_positioning: Premium (ILM) to mid (ILM-E, marketed as a cost-effective alternative with the same torque/kg as ILM). These are OEM frameless motor kits sold via the RoboDrive online shop (prices behind login/quote) and distributors; no public list pricing is published. Per-kit pricing is typically low-hundreds to ~1,000+ USD depending on size, but exact figures could not be confirmed from a credible source.

CubeMars is the robotics/actuator sister brand to T-Motor; both are Sanrui brands.
companies.focus: Quasi-direct-drive (QDD) integrated joint actuators, geared planetary servo modules, hollow-shaft planetary actuators, and frameless BLDC torque motors for legged, humanoid, exoskeleton, and collaborative robots.
companies.summary: CubeMars is the robotics power-systems brand of the Sanrui/T-Motor group, supplying highly-integrated planetary QDD joint actuators (AK series), exoskeleton/QDD modules (AKE series), hollow-shaft planetary joints (AKH series), and frameless inrunner torque motors (RI series) widely used in legged, humanoid, and exoskeleton robotics.
companies.price_positioning: Budget-to-mid. Frameless RI torque motors run ~$60-150 (RI50 $61.90, RI70 $123.90, RI100 $148.90); compact/mid AK and AKE integrated actuators ~$218-480; high-torque, high-ratio AKH and AK80-64 ~$600-890 (AKH70-16 $598.90, AKH70-48 $698.90, AK80-64 $889.90). Overall span roughly $60-$890 USD (official store list prices), positioned as affordable relative to harmonic-drive joints.

companies.parent: Nabtesco Corporation (TSE: 6268); Precision Reduction Gear (RV) products are made by the Nabtesco Precision Equipment Company division. Formed in 2003 by the merger of Teijin Seiki Co., Ltd. (precision gears, est. 1944) and NABCO Ltd. (est. 1925). The RV reducer technology descends from Teijin Seiki.
companies.focus: Precision two-stage cycloidal (RV / Rotate Vector) reduction gears, integrated cycloidal servo-actuators, and gearheads for industrial robot joints
companies.summary: Nabtesco is the world's largest manufacturer of precision cycloidal (RV) reduction gears, supplying roughly 60% of the global market for the reducers used in industrial robot joints, plus integrated cycloidal servo-actuators and gearheads.
companies.price_positioning: Premium industrial. Bare RV reduction-gear units typically run a few hundred to a few thousand USD each depending on size; integrated AF actuators and large RT units are higher (roughly $1,000 to $10,000+). Exact list prices are not published publicly (quote/distributor only), so per-model prices are null.

Component gear units roughly $300-$3,000+; integrated servo actuators commonly $1,000-$8,000+ depending on size, with the large SHA-58/65 units higher. Exact list prices not publicly available.

106x106x56mm, 42-pole. Rated speed 180 rpm, no-load 195 rpm, 380W. Torque constant 2.36 N.m/Arms, 300Hz response, -20 to +50C. Mid-large humanoid/quadruped joints.

Flagship/largest: 120x120x56mm, 42-pole, ~85.7 N.m/kg torque density. Rated speed 167 rpm, no-load 200 rpm, 700W. Default model in the open-source robstride Rust driver. For humanoid hip/knee and large legged robots.

companies.company: Genesis Robotics & Motion Technologies (Genesis Motion Solutions)
companies.parent: Subsidiary of Genesis Advanced Technology (GAT), Langley BC. Founded 2015 by Michael Gibney and James Klassen (Klassen = CTO/inventor). On April 9, 2018 Koch Chemicals Technology Group (KCTG), the industrial-technology unit of Koch Industries, closed a strategic and CONTROLLING investment in subsidiary Genesis Robotics, forming "Genesis Robotics & Motion Technologies." Now operates/markets as "Genesis Motion Solutions" (genesismotion.com); legacy domain genesisrobotics.com also resolves.
companies.focus: Gearless high-torque-density direct-drive rotary motors (LiveDrive LDX frameless, LDD housed, LDR torque motor) plus the Reflex compliant gearing system
companies.summary: Genesis is a Canadian motion-technology company, controlled by Koch Industries (via KCTG since 2018), that develops the patented LiveDrive gearless direct-drive torque motor (LDX frameless, LDD housed, LDR) and the Reflex high-performance gearing system, targeting robot joints, delta/collaborative robots, and precision machinery without harmonic or planetary gearheads.
companies.price_positioning: Premium / industrial; pricing is quote-based and not publicly listed. Positioned as a high-end gearless alternative to harmonic-drive joints. No public USD pricing was found for any model.

actuators.backdrivable: yes (true direct drive, zero backlash, fully backdrivable)
actuators.notes: Original LiveDrive direct-drive actuator/prototype unveiled ~2016-2018. Brushless permanent-magnet, gearless. Continuous 54 Nm / peak 120 Nm; 400 rpm top speed; 5.1 kg; OD 269 mm, ID 80 mm, axial thickness 16 mm. Torque-to-inertia 2,213 Nm/kg-m; power density 976 kW/m; forced-air cooled; ~0.2 arc-sec repeatability. All figures CONFIRMED via The Robot Report / IEEE Spectrum. Pitched as a harmonic-drive replacement for robot joints. This prototype's tech was later productized as the LDX/LDD families, but these exact numbers describe the prototype, not a current shipping model.

Patented frameless LiveDrive motor, unveiled at Automatica 2022; described as the world's highest torque-density direct-drive frameless motors. Available in multiple windings, diameters and stack lengths with bond/clamp/threaded-hub/through-hole integration. Only published headline claim is 'up to ~3x torque-to-mass vs other direct-drive motors.' Per-variant rated/peak torque, speed, weight, and dimensions are NOT published publicly and could not be retrieved (official site refused fetch), so all numeric fields are nulled. NOTE: the 269mm/16mm/2,213 Nm/kg-m figures sometimes associated with LDX actually belong to the original LiveDrive prototype and are NOT verified for LDX.

Current-catalog housed LiveDrive direct-drive rotary motor family that eliminates servo gearheads; marketed as the only direct-drive motors designed for delta robots. IP67 rated for light washdown (no oil/contamination). 'Up to ~3x torque-to-mass vs competing direct-drive motors.' Offered in multiple frame sizes/windings; per-variant torque/speed/weight not published publicly (nulled). The LDD 1800 Series (below) is the productized 180 mm member of this family.

actuators.encoder: 4 feedback options; Hiperface DSL one-cable technology; integrated holding brake (18 Nm holding torque at 24 VDC, 24 W)
actuators.notes: Productized 180 mm OD housed direct-drive actuator. CONFIRMED: 100 Nm PEAK torque capability (The Robot Report); IP67 raintight housing; 4 feedback options; one-cable technology via Hiperface DSL; integrated holding brake (18 Nm holding @ 24 VDC / 24 W per user manual); UL Registered; brushless permanent-magnet 3-phase synchronous; four standard sizes with various voltage levels; M23 power / M12 encoder connectors; PWM >=8 kHz; integrates with third-party servo drives; less than half the length of a typical servo-gearhead drivetrain. Rated/continuous torque, rated speed, and weight not published publicly (nulled). No public USD pricing.

Third LiveDrive motor family listed in the current Genesis Motion Solutions catalog alongside LDD (housed) and LDX (frameless); a direct-drive torque motor. ADDED in this revision (was missing from the draft). No published per-variant torque/speed/weight/dimension specs were retrievable (official site refused fetch), so all numeric fields are nulled. Existence confirmed via Genesis Motion Solutions catalog references.

actuators.type: compliant gearing (torque amplifier) — NOT a motor
actuators.notes: REFLEX high-performance gearing system: a backlash-free compliant torque amplifier with ~4x more engaged teeth than a conventional planetary gearbox (originally described as a plastic/polymer gearbox). Part of the technology Koch's 2018 venture set out to commercialize. NOT a motor/actuator and not clearly in the active commercial product menu as of 2026 — included for completeness; all numeric specs unverified/nulled.

companies.parent: Schaeffler AG (publicly listed, family-controlled group; brands include INA, FAG, LuK, IDAM). Robotics gears and torque motors are marketed via "Schaeffler Industrial Drives" (incorporating IDAM motor heritage). Confirmed: founded 1946 in Herzogenaurach by the Schaeffler brothers; INA = Industrie Nadellager; IDAM is part of the group.
companies.focus: Precision strain-wave (harmonic) gears, two-stage planetary integrated joint actuators, and frameless axial-flux PCB / torque motors for humanoid, cobot and lightweight-robotics joints, with high vertical integration (bearings, gears, motors, encoders, torque sensors, controllers in-house).
companies.summary: Schaeffler is a German motion-technology and bearings group that has entered humanoid and lightweight robotics with a vertically integrated actuator platform spanning precision strain-wave gears (RT series), a CES-2026 integrated planetary-gear humanoid joint actuator (60-250 Nm), and frameless axial-flux PCB torque motors (UPRS).
companies.price_positioning: Mid-to-premium industrial. Schaeffler does not publish list prices; components are quoted B2B as high-precision, high-durability industrial parts. No confirmed USD figures available for any model.

actuators.backdrivable: Yes - low back-drive resistance / high torque transparency; designed for smooth back-driving and sensitive force detection
actuators.notes: Schaeffler's flagship integrated humanoid joint actuator, shown for the first time at CES 2026 (pre-production). Combines a two-stage planetary gearbox + electric motor + encoder + controller in one compact, continuous-duty unit, all components made in-house. Published torque range 60-250 Nm (only the 250 Nm peak and 60 Nm low end are stated; per-unit rated torque not published). ~25-30 actuators per humanoid (hips, knees, shoulders). No public model designation, voltage, weight, comms, or price. CONFIRMED June 2026.

actuators.encoder: Precise encoder; optional integrated strain-wave torque sensor (RT1-T type)
actuators.notes: INFERRED, not a named SKU: a strain-wave-geared joint variant within Schaeffler's robotics portfolio (in-house BLDC motor + RT-series strain-wave gear + bearing + encoder + controller, optionally an RT1-T flex-spline torque sensor). Schaeffler markets the RT strain-wave gears and torque motors as building blocks for robot joints, but a distinct productized humanoid strain-wave actuator SKU is not separately published as of June 2026. No per-unit torque/speed/weight specs confirmed.

actuators.type: harmonic / strain-wave gear (gear unit, not motorized)
actuators.notes: High-Torque precision strain wave gear, sizes 14-32. Max torque up to 484 Nm (full RT range spans ~18-484 Nm); a high-torque envelope of ~25 to ~900 Nm is cited across sizes/ratios at 100/160. Exceeds the Standard-Torque RT2 by ~30% torque and ~40% service life. Variants HAT and CUP; versions CS, BHS, BMS, UHS. Gear unit only (not a motorized actuator). CONFIRMED June 2026.

actuators.type: harmonic / strain-wave gear with integrated torque sensor
actuators.encoder: Integrated strain-wave torque sensor (PVD-sputtered strain gauges, 16-bit, 5 kHz, +/-3% accuracy); adds no extra elasticity to drivetrain
actuators.notes: Sensorized RT1 with integrated flex-spline torque sensor. Sizes 14/17/25/32, ratios 100/160, max torque 36-484 Nm across sizes. Peer-reviewed unit RT1-H-17-100-UHS-T (size 17, ratio 100): main-range torque +/-70 Nm, collision torque +/-143 Nm, 16-bit sensor, 5 kHz sampling, +/-3% accuracy. CONFIRMED June 2026.

actuators.type: harmonic / strain-wave gear (gear unit, not motorized)
actuators.notes: Standard-Torque precision strain wave gear. Sizes 14/17/20/25/32, ratios 50/80/100/120/160, max torque 18-372 Nm. Broadest size/ratio portfolio in the RT range; ~30% lower torque and ~40% lower service life than RT1. Variant HAT; versions CS, BHS, BMS, UHS. Gear unit only. CONFIRMED June 2026.

Frameless axial-flux machines with PCB-configured coils for cobot/lightweight-robot joints. Four sizes 14/17/25/32, outer diameter 53-115 mm, axial length 21-33 mm. Near-zero cogging torque; speeds on average ~80% higher than conventional drives, higher torque density, lower weight. (diameter_mm/height_mm shown as the max of the published ranges: OD up to 115 mm, axial length up to 33 mm.) Per-size torque, voltage, and power not published in fetched sources. CONFIRMED June 2026.

companies.parent: Independent company; spinout of the Human Centered Robotics Lab at the University of Texas at Austin (co-founder/chief scientist Luis Sentis). Backed by Google, B Capital, Capital Factory; partners include NASA, NVIDIA, Texas Instruments, Mercedes-Benz.
companies.focus: High-force-density linear (ball-screw series-elastic) actuators and rotary quasi-direct-drive (QDD) actuators for humanoid/legged robots; built mostly as bespoke in-house joints for their own platforms rather than sold as a standalone catalog.
companies.summary: Apptronik is an Austin, Texas humanoid-robotics company (maker of the Apollo humanoid) that designs its own high-force-density linear series-elastic and rotary quasi-direct-drive actuators, of which only the P170 Orion linear actuator has been publicly sold/spec'd as a standalone product.
companies.price_positioning: Premium/research-grade; Apptronik does not publish actuator prices and no longer sells a public actuator catalog. The historical P170 Orion was offered only as part of an evaluation/eval-kit (research price, not listed; likely several thousand USD). Most actuators are integrated into platforms (Apollo est. ~$150k+ as a full robot), so per-actuator pricing is effectively N/A.

actuators.notes: Compact ball-screw series-elastic linear actuator (the only standalone Apptronik actuator with a published datasheet). Linear, NOT rotary, so force/stroke are the native ratings: continuous force 847 N (190 lbf), peak force 3200 N (719 lbf), max speed 27.7 cm/s, stroke 6.47 cm, ~80% max efficiency, 5 A continuous / 20 A peak, power density ~4 kN/kg. Sold mainly inside the Orion evaluation kit (1-DOF testbed, ROS/Linux, Axon controller). torque_*/speed_*_rpm left null because this is a linear (not rotary) actuator.

6th-generation custom high-force-density linear actuators used in Apollo's leg/arm joints (e.g. knee, elbow). Apptronik reports ~120 Nm/kg torque density and ~30% mass reduction for its proprietary high-force-density linear actuators, and uses TI motor-control/power-management ICs. Integrated into Apollo, not sold or individually spec'd. Specific per-joint force/torque/weight not publicly disclosed (left null).

Custom rotary quasi-direct-drive (low gear ratio) actuators used in Apollo's arm/upper-body joints for speed and dexterity. Part of Apptronik's stated 30+ unique in-house electric actuators (QDD, series-elastic, parallel-elastic, cable-driven, liquid-cooled). Not sold standalone; specific torque/speed/weight not officially published, so left null to avoid fabrication.

Quasi-direct-drive actuators packed into Apptronik's Astra upper-body humanoid (compact, mountable on any mobility base; uses elastic energy storage). Research/development platform actuators; not individually sold or spec'd. All numeric specs null (not publicly disclosed).

Liquid-cooled viscoelastic (series-elastic) actuators in the Draco 10-DOF biped (developed with Luis Sentis at UT-Austin HCRL). Designed to cut weight, increase payload and enable fast dynamic walking. Research platform actuators; not sold separately; numeric specs not publicly published (null).

Legacy P-series series-elastic actuator referenced in academic work (e.g. the P0 exoskeleton from Apptronik Systems). No full public datasheet for the P0 itself, so all numeric specs are null. Indicates a broader historical 'P-series' SEA family of which P170 Orion is the best-documented member.

companies.parent: Independent; founded and run by Josh Pieper. No parent company. "mjbots" and "moteus" are its own brands.
companies.focus: Open-source quasi-direct-drive (QDD) brushless actuators and compact CAN-FD brushless motor controllers (moteus) for legged/quadruped, humanoid, and dexterous robots
companies.summary: mjbots is a US-based open-source robotics hardware company that makes the moteus family of compact CAN-FD brushless motor controllers and the qdd100 quasi-direct-drive integrated joint actuator for dynamic legged and humanoid robots.
companies.price_positioning: Budget-to-mid for the robotics actuator market: moteus controllers run roughly $69-$175 each (c1 $69, r4.11 $94, n1 $149, x1 $175), and the qdd100 integrated QDD actuator is ~$819-$879. Notably cheaper than comparable QDD joints from larger vendors, positioned for hobbyist/research/startup robotics.

actuators.encoder: Integrated absolute magnetic encoder (on-axis), rotor-side; output-side via moteus controller
actuators.backdrivable: Yes (low-reduction quasi-direct-drive; no formal backdrive-torque figure published)
actuators.notes: mjbots' flagship quasi-direct-drive integrated joint actuator built around a moteus controller and a planetary geartrain (6:1 per mjbots blog; not stated on current beta-3 store page). Thermal-limited torque: 16 Nm <1s peak, 10 Nm for 60s, 6 Nm for 400s, 3.3 Nm continuous/indefinite (used as rated). Peak speed 3,600 dps @36V (=600 rpm) / 2,300 dps @24V (~383 rpm). 5Mbps CAN-FD. Backlash +-0.25 deg. Currently sold as 'beta 3'; out of stock with MOQ 50 as of June 2026.

actuators.encoder: Integrated absolute magnetic encoder (6mm diametric disc magnet included); STM32G4 170 MHz MCU
actuators.notes: Newest moteus controller (released May 2025). Highest continuous output of the line: 25A continuous phase current without cooling, 62A with thermal management; 120A peak. ~1.3kW peak electrical @36V. Adds an RS422 connector in addition to 5Mbps CAN-FD. 56x56x10mm, 23.7g. Open-source firmware (Apache 2.0). Not a geared actuator.

actuators.encoder: Integrated absolute magnetic encoder (on-board); STM32G4 170 MHz MCU
actuators.notes: Compact brushless servo controller (not a geared actuator). 100A peak phase current; 9A/26A continuous without/with thermal management; ~2kW peak electrical @36V; 46x46x8mm board, 14.6g. Same firmware/CAN interface as r4.11; higher voltage ceiling (<=12S). Open-source (Apache 2.0).

actuators.encoder: Integrated absolute magnetic encoder (diametric magnet included); STM32G4 170 MHz MCU
actuators.notes: Long-standing flagship brushless servo controller (not a geared actuator). 100A peak phase current; 12A/32A continuous without/with thermal management; ~900W peak @30V; 46x53mm board, 14.2g, daisy-chainable 5Mbps CAN-FD. Operating temp -40 to 85C. Open-source firmware (Apache 2.0). The controller at the core of the qdd100.

actuators.encoder: Integrated absolute magnetic encoder; STM32G4 170 MHz MCU
actuators.notes: Smallest/lowest-power moteus controller (not a geared actuator), for low-cost, low-power joints e.g. dexterous hands/small robots. 20A peak phase current; 5A/14A continuous without/with thermal management; ~250W peak @28V; 38x38x9mm, 8.9g. Operating temp -40 to 85C. Open-source (Apache 2.0).

companies.parent: Spin-off of the German Aerospace Center (DLR), founded 2003 by Norbert Sporer; technology derived from DLR's torque-sensing / lightweight-robot work. Independent GmbH (confirmed via DLR spin-off page and Sensodrive's own "20 years" page).
companies.focus: Torque-controlled integrated robotic joint actuators (Harmonic Drive strain-wave gearbox + integrated torque sensor + BLDC motor + integrated controller + brake) for sensitive/cobot, medical and force-feedback robotics
companies.summary: Sensodrive is a German DLR spin-off that builds the SensoJoint family of fully integrated, torque-controlled robotic joint actuators combining a proprietary integrated torque sensor, Harmonic Drive strain-wave gearbox, BLDC motor, controller and brake; in March 2025 its SensoJoints became the first safety-certified (TUV Sud; ISO 13849 / EN 61800-5-2 / IEC 61508) torque-controlled robot drives.
companies.price_positioning: Premium / high-end industrial. No public list pricing; sold on a quote/custom-configuration basis to OEMs. Exact figures not published anywhere credible.

companies.parent: Tinymovr is the product brand of MotionLayer P.C. (Greece). The tinymovr.com storefront 301-redirects to motionlayer.company, where all Tinymovr products are sold. Project started by Yannis Chatzikonstantinou on Hackaday.io in 2019.
companies.focus: Open-source compact FOC BLDC motor controllers (R-series and M-series) with onboard MPS MA702 absolute encoders and CAN bus, plus one lightweight integrated planetary robot-joint actuator (Axion R1)
companies.summary: Tinymovr (a brand of MotionLayer P.C., Komotini, Greece) makes affordable open-source 3-phase FOC BLDC motor controllers with integrated MPS MA702 absolute encoders and CAN/UART/SPI connectivity, plus one lightweight integrated robot-joint actuator (Axion R1) built around its M5 controller and a 10:1 planetary gearmotor.
companies.price_positioning: Budget/maker-tier. Controllers EUR 88 (R5.3) to EUR 98 (M5.2) (~$95-106); integrated Axion R1 actuator EUR 169 (~$182); servo kits EUR 169 (~$182); starter kit EUR 129 (~$140). Well below industrial QDD actuator pricing.

actuators.encoder: Onboard MPS MA702 12-bit absolute magnetic angle sensor (same as Tinymovr controllers; not explicitly named on Axion spec page but uses the integrated M5)
actuators.backdrivable: Not explicitly stated; low-ratio (10:1) planetary with 0.1 deg backlash, so likely partially backdrivable
actuators.notes: Lightweight integrated brushless actuator combining a Tinymovr M5 controller with a GIM4305 motor + 10:1 planetary reducer (0.1 deg backlash). Continuous 1 Nm / peak 3 Nm; max output speed 320 rpm @24V (this is rated/max, NOT no-load); 50 W continuous, 0.5 W idle; max phase current 8.0 A. Torque density ~20 Nm/kg. Interfaces: CAN Bus 1 Mbps (dual ports for daisy-chaining), UART, SPI, SWD. ⌀53 x 26 mm, 160 g. Currently SOLD OUT; listed stock are 'used engineering samples' (low-volume/early product). NOTE: the draft's 'RS485' and 'up to 100 W peak' are NOT in official specs and were removed.

actuators.encoder: Onboard MPS MA702 absolute magnetic angle sensor
actuators.notes: Ready-to-use direct-drive servo bundle: a Tinymovr R5 controller paired with a brushless motor on an aluminum bracket. A NEMA-mount variant (Servo Kit R5.2 NEMA, same EUR 169 price) also exists. Sold as a bundle, not a sealed actuator; specific motor torque/speed are motor-dependent and not published on the store page. Both variants currently sold out. RS485 removed (not a supported interface).

actuators.encoder: Onboard MPS MA702 absolute magnetic angle sensor
actuators.notes: Not a standalone actuator — a compact open-source FOC BLDC motor CONTROLLER (36x40mm, 10 g). Max continuous phase current 25.0 A (cooling-dependent; the draft's 40 A figure was INCORRECT). 12-38V, position/velocity/torque modes. Listed as the building block of Tinymovr R-series servo kits. Interfaces: 2x CAN 1 Mbps (daisy-chain), UART, SPI, plus AUX/SWD. RS485 removed (not supported).

actuators.encoder: Onboard MPS MA702 high-resolution absolute angle sensor
actuators.notes: Not a standalone actuator — a 29.5x29.5mm, 8 g compact open-source FOC BLDC motor CONTROLLER for gimbal-style and lightweight robotic-joint motors. Continuous phase current 6.0 A (exact; draft said '5-6A'), 12-38V. This is the controller embedded inside the Axion R1 actuator. Interfaces: CAN 1 Mbps (dual ports, daisy-chain), UART, SPI (via JST-SH 8-pin), SWD (JST-SH 4-pin). RS485 removed (not supported).

companies.company: Allied Motion (Allied Motion Technologies, an Allient company)

The corporation was founded in January 1939 in Denver, CO as Hathaway Instruments Company (founder Claude Hathaway), incorporated as a public company in 1962 as Hathaway Corporation, renamed Allied Motion Technologies Inc. in November 2002, and renamed Allient Inc. on August 23, 2023, while retaining "Allied Motion" as a product/brand name.
companies.focus: Frameless brushless direct-drive torque motors (kit rotor/stator sets) and slotless motors for robot joints, arms and gimbals — not pre-geared integrated QDD joints.
companies.summary: Allied Motion (a brand of parent Allient Inc.) is a US motion-control maker supplying high-torque-density frameless brushless torque-motor kits and slotless motors that OEMs integrate directly into robot, cobot, surgical-robot and humanoid joints.
companies.price_positioning: Mid-to-premium industrial/medical-grade OEM motor components; sold as engineered kit motors with custom windings rather than off-the-shelf priced units. Public list pricing is not published (quote-based); no credible per-model USD found, so prices are null.

actuators.notes: Family/brand entry. Revo1 is an in-house high-torque-density brushless DC direct-drive servo developed by Halodi (~2018), marketed as the world's highest torque-to-weight direct-drive motor and tailored for low-gear-ratio robotics. Used in Halodi/1X EVE and NEO humanoids. Offered in multiple sizes (distributor SKUs REVO1-15 and REVO1-30). Only the medium size has fully recoverable published numbers.

Medium-size Revo1 disclosed by Halodi engineer at ICRA 2018 (confirmed verbatim): 20 Nm peak torque, 0.55 kg, 103 mm outer diameter, ~15 mm axial length, ~204 W power draw at stall while holding 10 Nm. Implied torque density ~36 Nm/kg. Pancake/frameless form factor. Corresponds to distributor SKU REVO1-15 (also 20 Nm peak). The 204 W figure is power draw at a 10 Nm stall condition, not a continuous rating.

Distributor (Future Robotix / Motion Control Products) SKU for the smaller Revo1 size. Peak torque = 20 Nm (confirmed via current distributor search snippet), matching the ICRA 2018 medium-unit disclosure (0.55 kg, 103 mm dia, ~15 mm length). Future Robotix domain is now parked/for-sale; continuous torque, voltage, power, encoder, comms, and price are not publicly verifiable and are left null.

Larger Revo1 size SKU listed by distributor Future Robotix / Motion Control Products. Peak torque = 40 Nm (CORRECTION: confirmed via current distributor search snippet; draft left this null). The draft's inference that '-30' denotes ~30 mm axial length is NOT supported — the suffix appears to track torque/size class (20 Nm for -15 vs 40 Nm for -30), so height_mm is nulled. Continuous torque, speed, voltage, power, weight, diameter, encoder, comms, IP, and price are not publicly verifiable (distributor domain dead, no official datasheet public) and are left null.
